title_en: Biosecurity Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of maintaining national security, preventing and responding to biosecurity risks, safeguarding the life and health of the people, protecting biological resources and the ecological environment, promoting the healthy development of biotechnology, advancing the building of a community with a shared future for mankind, and realizing the harmonious coexistence of human and nature.

Article 3 Biosecurity is an important component of national security. To maintain biosecurity, the holistic approach to national security shall be implemented, development and security shall be coordinated, and the principles of putting people first, risk prevention, classified management, and coordinated cooperation shall be adhered to.

Article 4 The leadership of the Communist Party of China over national biosecurity work shall be upheld, a national biosecurity leadership system shall be established and improved, the national biosecurity risk prevention and control system and governance system shall be strengthened, and the national biosecurity governance capacity shall be enhanced.

Article 5 The State encourages innovation in biotechnology, strengthens the construction of biosecurity infrastructure and the building of biological science and technology talent teams, supports the development of the bio-industry, uses innovation to drive the improvement of biological science and technology levels, and enhances biosecurity assurance capabilities.

Article 6 The State strengthens international cooperation in the field of biosecurity, fulfills the obligations stipulated in international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, supports participation in biological science and technology exchanges and cooperation and international rescue in biosecurity incidents, actively participates in the research and formulation of international rules on biosecurity, and promotes the improvement of global biosecurity governance.

Article 7 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall strengthen the publicity and popularization of biosecurity laws, regulations and knowledge, guide grassroots self-governing organizations and social organizations to carry out publicity on biosecurity laws, regulations and knowledge, and promote the enhancement of biosecurity awareness in the whole society.
Relevant scientific research institutions, medical institutions, and other enterprises and public institutions shall incorporate biosecurity laws, regulations and knowledge into education and training content, and strengthen the cultivation of biosecurity awareness and ethical awareness among students and practitioners.
News media shall conduct public interest publicity on biosecurity laws, regulations and knowledge, exercise public opinion supervision over illegal acts against biosecurity, and enhance the public's sense of social responsibility for maintaining biosecurity.

Article 8 No entity or individual may endanger biosecurity.
Any entity or individual has the right to report acts that endanger biosecurity; the department that receives the report shall handle it in a timely manner according to law.

Article 9 Entities and individuals that have made outstanding contributions to biosecurity work shall be commended and rewarded by people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments in accordance with state regulations.

Article 10 The central national security leadership body shall be responsible for decision-making and deliberative coordination on national biosecurity work, study, formulate and guide the implementation of the national biosecurity strategy and relevant major policies, coordinate major matters and important work on national biosecurity, and establish a national biosecurity work coordination mechanism.
Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall establish biosecurity work coordination mechanisms to organize, coordinate, supervise and promote biosecurity-related work within their respective administrative regions.

Article 11 The national biosecurity work coordination mechanism shall be composed of the competent departments of the State Council for health, agriculture and rural affairs, science and technology, foreign affairs, and other relevant departments, as well as relevant military organs, to analyze and assess the national biosecurity situation, organize, coordinate, and supervise the promotion of national biosecurity-related work. The national biosecurity work coordination mechanism shall establish an office to be responsible for its daily work.
Member units of the national biosecurity work coordination mechanism and other relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for biosecurity-related work in accordance with their respective duties.

Article 12 The national biosecurity work coordination mechanism shall establish an expert committee to provide decision-making consultation for national biosecurity strategy research, policy formulation and implementation.
Relevant departments of the State Council shall organize the establishment of biosecurity technical consultation expert committees in relevant fields and industries to provide technical support such as consultation, evaluation, and argumentation for biosecurity work.

Article 13 Local people's governments at all levels shall be responsible for biosecurity work within their respective administrative regions.
Relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for biosecurity-related work in accordance with their respective duties.
Grassroots self-governing organizations shall assist local people's governments and relevant departments in carrying out biosecurity risk prevention and control, emergency response, and publicity and education.
Relevant entities and individuals shall cooperate in carrying out biosecurity risk prevention and control, emergency response, and other work.

Article 14 The State shall establish a biosecurity risk monitoring and early warning system. The national biosecurity work coordination mechanism shall organize the establishment of a national biosecurity risk monitoring and early warning system to improve the ability to identify and analyze biosecurity risks.

Article 16 The State shall establish a biosecurity information sharing system. The national biosecurity work coordination mechanism shall organize the establishment of a unified national biosecurity information platform, and the relevant departments shall submit biosecurity data, information, and other materials to the national biosecurity information platform to achieve information sharing.

Article 17 The State shall establish a biosecurity information release system. Major biosecurity information, such as the overall biosecurity situation of the State, major biosecurity risk warning information, major biosecurity incidents and their investigation and handling information, shall be released by the member units of the national biosecurity work coordination mechanism in accordance with their respective duties; other biosecurity information shall be released by the relevant departments of the State Council and the people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments in accordance with their respective functions and powers.
No entity or individual may fabricate or disseminate false biosecurity information.

Article 18 The State shall establish a biosecurity catalog and list system. The State Council and its relevant departments shall, based on the needs of biosecurity work, formulate and publish catalogs or lists of materials, equipment, technologies, activities, important biological resources data, infectious diseases, animal and plant epidemics, invasive alien species, etc., related to biosecurity, and make dynamic adjustments.

Article 19 The State shall establish a biosecurity standards system. The standardization administrative department of the State Council and other relevant departments of the State Council shall, in accordance with their respective duties, formulate and improve relevant standards in the field of biosecurity.
The national biosecurity work coordination mechanism shall organize relevant departments to strengthen the coordination and connection of biosecurity standards in different fields, and establish and improve the biosecurity standards system.

Article 20 The State shall establish a biosecurity review system. Major matters and activities in the biological field that affect or may affect national security shall be subject to biosecurity review by the relevant departments of the State Council to effectively prevent and mitigate biosecurity risks.

Article 21 The State shall establish an emergency response system for biosecurity that features unified leadership, coordinated action, and orderly and efficient response.
Relevant departments of the State Council shall organize the formulation of emergency plans for biosecurity incidents in relevant fields and industries, and carry out emergency drills, emergency response, emergency rescue, and post-incident recovery in accordance with the emergency plans and unified deployment.
Local people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall formulate, organize, guide, and supervise relevant enterprises and public institutions in formulating emergency plans for biosecurity incidents, strengthen emergency preparedness, personnel training, and emergency drills, and carry out emergency response, emergency rescue, and post-incident recovery for biosecurity incidents.
The Chinese People's Liberation Army and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force shall, in accordance with the orders of the Central Military Commission, participate in emergency response and emergency rescue for biosecurity incidents according to law.

Article 22 The State shall establish a biosecurity incident investigation and traceability system. Where a major emerging or sudden infectious disease, animal or plant epidemic, or a biosecurity incident of unknown cause occurs, the national biosecurity work coordination mechanism shall organize investigations and traceability to determine the nature of the incident, comprehensively assess its impact, and put forward opinions and suggestions.

Article 23 The State shall establish a national准入 system for animals, plants, animal and plant products, and high-risk biological factors that are brought into the country for the first time or after suspension of import.
Personnel, means of transport, containers, goods, articles, packaging materials entering or leaving the country, and the discharge of ballast water from international ships shall comply with the biosecurity management requirements of China.
Customs shall handle biosecurity risks discovered in import, export, and transit according to law. Persons, means of transport, goods, articles, etc., assessed as having a high biosecurity risk shall be imported through designated border ports and be subject to strict risk prevention and control measures.

Article 24 The State shall establish a system for responding to major biosecurity incidents abroad. Where a major biosecurity incident occurs abroad, Customs shall take urgent biosecurity prevention and control measures according to law, strengthen document verification, increase inspection ratios, and suspend the entry of relevant personnel, means of transport, goods, articles, etc. When necessary, with the approval of the State Council, measures such as temporarily closing relevant ports or sealing relevant borders may be taken.

Article 25 Relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall carry out biosecurity supervision and inspection according to law; the entities and individuals under inspection shall cooperate, truthfully explain the situation, and provide materials, and shall not refuse or obstruct.
For supervision and inspection work involving high professional and technical requirements and difficult law enforcement operations, biosecurity professional and technical personnel shall participate.

Article 27 The competent departments of the State Council for health, agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and grassland, customs, and ecological environment shall establish monitoring networks for emerging or sudden infectious diseases, animal and plant epidemics, import and export quarantine, and environmental safety of biotechnology, organize the layout and construction of monitoring stations, improve monitoring information reporting systems, carry out active monitoring and pathogen detection, and incorporate them into the national biosecurity risk monitoring and early warning system.

Article 28 Disease prevention and control institutions, animal epidemic prevention and control institutions, and plant pest prevention and control institutions (hereinafter collectively referred to as professional institutions) shall conduct active monitoring of infectious diseases, animal and plant epidemics, and unexplained diseases included in the monitoring scope, collect, analyze, and report monitoring information, and predict the occurrence and epidemic trends of emerging or sudden infectious diseases and animal and plant epidemics.
Relevant departments of the State Council, local people's governments at or above the county level, and their relevant departments shall promptly issue warnings based on predictions and their respective functions and powers, and take corresponding prevention and control measures.

Article 29 Any entity or individual that discovers an infectious disease or an animal or plant epidemic shall promptly report it to a medical institution, relevant professional institution, or department.
Medical institutions, professional institutions, and their staff who discover an infectious disease, an animal or plant epidemic, or an unexplained cluster of diseases shall promptly report and take protective measures.
For matters that shall be reported according to law, no entity or individual may conceal, make false reports, delay reports, omit reports, instruct others to conceal, make false reports, or delay reports, or obstruct others from reporting.

Article 30 The State shall establish a joint prevention and control mechanism for major emerging or sudden infectious diseases and animal and plant epidemics.
Where a major emerging or sudden infectious disease or animal or plant epidemic occurs, control measures shall be taken promptly in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, regulations, and emergency plans; the competent departments of the State Council for health, agriculture and rural affairs, and forestry and grassland shall immediately organize epidemic consultation and assessment, report the conclusions of the consultation and assessment to the central national security leadership body and the State Council, and notify other member units of the national biosecurity work coordination mechanism and other relevant departments of the State Council.
Where a major emerging or sudden infectious disease or animal or plant epidemic occurs, local people's governments at all levels shall uniformly perform the duties of epidemic prevention and control within their respective administrative regions, strengthen organizational leadership, carry out mass prevention and control and medical treatment, and mobilize and encourage social forces to participate in epidemic prevention and control work according to law and in an orderly manner.

Article 31 The State shall strengthen the capacity building for joint prevention and control of infectious diseases and animal and plant epidemics at borders and ports, establish an international cooperation network for the prevention and control of infectious diseases and animal and plant epidemics, and detect and control major emerging or sudden infectious diseases and animal and plant epidemics at an early stage.
Article 32 The State shall protect wildlife, strengthen animal epidemic prevention, and prevent the spread of zoonotic infectious diseases.

Article 33 The State shall strengthen the management of the use and residues of antimicrobial drugs such as antibiotics, and support basic research and scientific and technological efforts to address antimicrobial resistance.
The competent health departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the guidance and supervision of rational drug use in medical institutions, and take measures to prevent the irrational use of antimicrobial drugs. The competent departments of agriculture and rural affairs, and forestry and grassland of people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the guidance and supervision of rational drug use in agricultural production, and take measures to prevent the irrational use of antimicrobial drugs and reduce their residues in the agricultural production environment.
The competent departments of the State Council for health, agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and grassland, ecological environment, and the drug regulatory authority shall, in accordance with their respective duties, assess the harm of antimicrobial drug residues to human health and the environment, and establish an indicator evaluation system for antimicrobial drug pollutants.

Article 34 The State shall strengthen the safety management of biotechnology research, development, and application activities, and prohibit biotechnology research, development, and application activities that endanger public health, damage biological resources, destroy ecosystems and biodiversity, or otherwise jeopardize biosecurity.
Biotechnology research, development, and application activities shall comply with ethical principles.

Article 35 Entities engaged in biotechnology research, development, and application activities shall be responsible for the safety of their own biotechnology research, development, and application, take biosecurity risk prevention and control measures, formulate work systems such as biosecurity training, follow-up inspections, and regular reporting, and strengthen process management.

Article 36 The State implements classified management of biotechnology research and development activities. Based on the degree of risk of harm to public health, industry and agriculture, ecological environment, etc., biotechnology research and development activities are classified into three categories: high-risk, medium-risk, and low-risk.
The risk classification standards and catalogs for biotechnology research and development activities shall be formulated, adjusted, and published by the competent departments of the State Council for science and technology, health, agriculture and rural affairs, etc., in accordance with their respective duties, in conjunction with other relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 37 Those engaged in biotechnology research and development activities shall comply with the national safety management norms for biotechnology research and development.
Those engaged in biotechnology research and development activities shall assess the risk category, closely monitor changes in risks, and take timely response measures.

Article 38 High-risk and medium-risk biotechnology research and development activities shall be conducted by legal person organizations established according to law within the territory of China, and shall obtain approval or undergo filing according to law.
Those engaged in high-risk and medium-risk biotechnology research and development activities shall conduct risk assessments, formulate risk prevention and control plans and biosecurity incident emergency plans, and reduce the risks associated with the implementation of such research and development activities.

Article 39 The State implements traceability management for important equipment and special biological factors related to biosecurity. The purchase or introduction of important equipment and special biological factors included in the control list shall be registered to ensure traceability, and shall be reported to the relevant departments of the State Council for filing.
Individuals may not purchase or possess important equipment and special biological factors included in the control list.

Article 40 Clinical research on new biomedical technologies shall undergo ethical review and be conducted within medical institutions with corresponding conditions; human clinical research operations shall be performed by health professional and technical personnel meeting the corresponding qualifications.

Article 41 Relevant departments of the State Council shall conduct follow-up evaluations on biotechnology application activities according to law, and if biosecurity risks are discovered, they shall promptly take effective remedial and control measures.

Article 42 The State shall strengthen the management of biosecurity in pathogenic microorganism laboratories, and formulate unified laboratory biosecurity standards. Pathogenic microorganism laboratories shall comply with national biosecurity standards and requirements.
Those engaged in pathogenic microorganism experimental activities shall strictly comply with relevant national standards, laboratory technical specifications, and operating procedures, and take safety precautions.

Article 43 The State implements classified management of pathogenic microorganisms based on their infectivity and the degree of harm to individuals or groups of humans and animals after infection.
Activities involving the collection, storage, and transport of samples of highly pathogenic or suspected highly pathogenic pathogenic microorganisms shall meet the corresponding conditions and comply with biosecurity management norms. Specific measures shall be formulated by the competent departments of the State Council for health, and agriculture and rural affairs.

Article 44 The establishment of a pathogenic microorganism laboratory shall be approved or filed according to law.
Individuals may not establish pathogenic microorganism laboratories or engage in pathogenic microorganism experimental activities.

Article 45 The State implements grade-based management of pathogenic microorganism laboratories based on the level of biosecurity protection required for the pathogenic microorganisms.
Pathogenic microorganism experimental activities shall be conducted in laboratories of the corresponding grade. Low-grade pathogenic microorganism laboratories may not conduct pathogenic microorganism experimental activities that, according to the national pathogenic microorganism catalog, shall be conducted in high-grade pathogenic microorganism laboratories.

Article 46 High-grade pathogenic microorganism laboratories conducting experimental activities involving highly pathogenic or suspected highly pathogenic pathogenic microorganisms shall obtain approval from the competent health or agriculture and rural affairs departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level, and shall report the status of the experimental activities to the approving department.
For pathogenic microorganisms that have not yet been discovered in China or have been declared eradicated, relevant experimental activities shall not be conducted without approval.

Article 47 Pathogenic microorganism laboratories shall take measures to strengthen the management of experimental animals, prevent the escape of experimental animals, carry out harmless treatment of used experimental animals in accordance with state regulations, and achieve traceability of experimental animals. The circulation of used experimental animals into the market is prohibited.
Pathogenic microorganism laboratories shall strengthen the management of waste from experimental activities, dispose of wastewater, exhaust gas, and other waste according to law, and take measures to prevent pollution.

Article 48 The entity establishing a pathogenic microorganism laboratory shall be responsible for the biosecurity management of the laboratory, formulate scientific and strict management systems, regularly inspect the implementation of relevant biosecurity provisions, and inspect, maintain, and update laboratory facilities, equipment, materials, etc., to ensure their compliance with national standards.
The legal representative of the entity establishing the pathogenic microorganism laboratory and the person in charge of the laboratory shall be responsible for the biosecurity of the laboratory.

Article 49 The entity establishing a pathogenic microorganism laboratory shall establish and improve a security and protection system, take security and protection measures, and ensure the safety of the laboratory and its pathogenic microorganisms.
The State shall strengthen the security and protection of high-grade pathogenic microorganism laboratories. High-grade pathogenic microorganism laboratories shall accept supervision and guidance from public security organs and other departments regarding laboratory security and protection work, and strictly prevent the leakage, loss, theft, or robbery of highly pathogenic pathogenic microorganisms.
The State shall establish an entry review system for personnel entering high-grade pathogenic microorganism laboratories. Personnel entering high-grade pathogenic microorganism laboratories shall be approved by the person in charge of the laboratory. Approval shall not be granted if it may affect laboratory biosecurity; for those approved to enter, safety and security measures shall be taken.

Article 50 The entity establishing a pathogenic microorganism laboratory shall formulate an emergency plan for biosecurity incidents, and regularly organize personnel training and emergency drills. Where a high-grade pathogenic microorganism leaks, is lost, stolen, or robbed, or other biosecurity risks occur, control measures shall be taken promptly in accordance with the provisions of the emergency plan, and reports shall be made in accordance with state regulations.

Article 51 The provincial people's government where the pathogenic microorganism laboratory is located and its competent health department shall strengthen the allocation of medical resources for infectious diseases in the location of the laboratory, and improve the capacity for medical treatment of infectious diseases.

Article 52 The biosafety management of production workshops involving the operation of pathogenic microorganisms by enterprises shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions on relevant pathogenic microorganism laboratories and other biosafety management norms.
The construction and management of biosafety laboratories involving the operation of biological toxins, plant pests, and other biological agents shall be implemented by reference to the provisions on relevant pathogenic microorganism laboratories.

Article 53 The State shall strengthen the management and supervision of activities such as the collection, preservation, utilization, and provision to foreign parties of human genetic resources and biological resources, and shall ensure the security of human genetic resources and biological resources.
The State shall have sovereignty over human genetic resources and biological resources within its territory.

Article 54 The State shall conduct surveys of human genetic resources and biological resources.
The competent health department of the State Council shall organize and carry out the survey of human genetic resources within China, and shall formulate measures for the declaration and registration of important genetic pedigrees and human genetic resources of specific regions.
The competent departments of the State Council for health, science and technology, natural resources, ecological environment, agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and grassland, and traditional Chinese medicine shall, according to their respective responsibilities, organize and carry out surveys of biological resources and formulate measures for the declaration and registration of important biological resources.

Article 55 The collection, preservation, utilization, and provision to foreign parties of human genetic resources within China shall comply with ethical principles, and shall not harm public health, national security, or social public interests.

Article 57 Where human genetic resource information within China is provided or made available for use to foreign organizations, individuals, or institutions established or actually controlled by them, the provider shall report in advance to the competent health department of the State Council and submit a backup of the information.

Article 58 The collection, preservation, utilization, and transport out of the territory of China of rare, endangered, or endemic species and their genetic resources, including individuals, organs, tissues, cells, genes, and other materials that can be used for regeneration or reproduction and inheritance, shall comply with relevant laws and regulations.
Foreign organizations, individuals, and institutions established or actually controlled by them shall obtain approval according to law when acquiring and utilizing biological resources within China.

Article 59 Conducting international scientific research cooperation using biological resources within China shall obtain approval according to law.
When conducting international scientific research cooperation using human genetic resources and biological resources within China, it shall be ensured that Chinese entities and their researchers participate fully and substantively throughout the research process and share relevant rights and interests according to law.

Article 60 The State shall strengthen the prevention and response to the invasion of alien species and protect biodiversity. The competent department of agriculture and rural affairs of the State Council shall, together with other relevant departments of the State Council, formulate a list of invasive alien species and management measures.
The relevant departments of the State Council shall, according to their respective responsibilities, strengthen the investigation, monitoring, early warning, control, assessment, removal, and ecological restoration of invasive alien species.
No unit or individual shall, without approval, arbitrarily introduce, release, or discard alien species.

Article 61 The State shall take all necessary measures to prevent bioterrorism and the threat of biological weapons.
No person shall develop, manufacture, or otherwise acquire, store, possess, or use biological weapons.
No person shall in any manner instigate, fund, or assist others to develop, manufacture, or otherwise acquire biological weapons.

Article 62 The relevant departments of the State Council shall formulate, amend, and publish a list of organisms, biotoxins, equipment, or technologies that may be used for bioterrorism activities or the manufacture of biological weapons, and shall strengthen supervision to prevent their use for the manufacture of biological weapons or for terrorist purposes.

Article 63 The relevant departments of the State Council and relevant military organs shall, according to their respective responsibilities, strengthen the monitoring and investigation of activities such as the entry-exit, import-export, acquisition, manufacture, transfer, and release of organisms, biotoxins, equipment, or technologies that may be used for bioterrorism or the manufacture of biological weapons, and shall take necessary preventive and disposal measures.

Article 64 The relevant departments of the State Council, the provincial people's governments, and their relevant departments shall be responsible for organizing the treatment and resettlement of personnel, environmental disinfection, ecological restoration, safety monitoring, and restoration of social order after a bioterrorist attack or biological weapon attack.
The relevant departments of the State Council, the provincial people's governments, and their relevant departments shall effectively guide public opinion to report bioterrorist attacks and biological weapon attacks scientifically and accurately, shall timely issue information on evacuation, transfer, and emergency shelter, and shall conduct long-term environmental monitoring and health monitoring of areas and personnel contaminated during the emergency response and recovery process.

Article 65 The State shall organize and carry out investigations of biological weapons left over from wars within the territory of China, as well as their harmful results and potential impacts.
The State shall organize the construction of facilities for the storage and disposal of biological weapons left over from wars, and shall ensure the safe disposal of such weapons.

Article 67 The State shall take measures to support scientific and technological research on biosafety, strengthen research on biosafety risk prevention and control technologies, integrate advantageous forces and resources, establish a joint research mechanism with multi-disciplinary and multi-departmental collaborative innovation, promote the output and transformation and application of core key technologies and major defense products for biosafety, and improve the scientific and technological support capability for biosafety.

Article 68 The State shall make an overall layout of national biosafety infrastructure construction. The relevant departments of the State Council shall, according to their respective responsibilities, accelerate the construction of national strategic resource platforms for biosafety in aspects such as bioinformatics, preservation of human genetic resources, preservation of bacterial (virus) strains, preservation of animal and plant genetic resources, and high-level pathogenic microorganism laboratories, establish a sharing and utilization mechanism, and provide strategic guarantee and support for scientific and technological innovation in biosafety.

Article 69 The relevant departments of the State Council shall, according to their respective responsibilities, strengthen the training of talents in basic bioscience research and professional technical personnel in the biological field, and promote the construction of basic bioscience disciplines and scientific research.
Practitioners in important positions of national biosafety infrastructure shall possess qualifications that meet the requirements, shall file relevant information with the relevant departments of the State Council, and shall receive post training.

Article 70 The State shall strengthen the material reserves for prevention and control of biosafety risks such as major emerging infectious diseases and animal and plant epidemics.
The State shall strengthen the research, development, and technical reserves of emergency drugs, equipment, and other materials for biosafety. The relevant departments of the State Council shall, according to their respective responsibilities, implement relevant measures for the research, development, and technical reserves of emergency drugs, equipment, and other materials for biosafety.
The relevant departments of the State Council and the local people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall ensure the production, supply, and allocation of medical rescue equipment, treatment drugs, medical devices, and other materials required for emergency response to biosafety incidents; the competent transport department shall timely organize and coordinate transport operators to give priority to transportation.

Article 71 The State shall provide effective protective measures and medical security for personnel engaged in high-risk biosafety work such as experimental activities involving highly pathogenic microorganisms and on-site disposal of biosafety incidents.

Article 72 Where a staff member performing biosafety management duties abuses power, neglects duty, practices favoritism or fraud, or commits any other illegal act in biosafety work in violation of the provisions of this Law, the said staff member shall be given a sanction according to law.

Article 73 Where a medical institution, professional institution, or any of their staff members, in violation of the provisions of this Law, conceals, falsely reports, delays reporting, or omits reporting, instigates others to conceal, falsely report, or delay reporting, or obstructs others from reporting infectious diseases, animal or plant epidemics, or clusters of diseases of unknown cause, the relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction and give a warning; the legal representative, main person in charge, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law, and may be suspended from practicing activities for a certain period until their relevant practice certificates are revoked according to law.
Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, fabricates or disseminates false biosafety information, constituting an act violating public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security punishment according to law.

Article 74 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, engages in research, development, or application activities of biotechnology prohibited by the State, the competent departments of health, science and technology, and agriculture and rural affairs of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective responsibilities, order cessation of the illegal act, confiscate the illegal gains, technical materials, and items such as tools, equipment, and raw materials used for the illegal act, impose a fine of not less than one million yuan but not more than ten million yuan; if the illegal gains are more than one million yuan, impose a fine of not less than ten times but not more than twenty times the illegal gains; and may, according to law, prohibit the person from engaging in corresponding biotechnological research, development, and application activities for a certain period and revoke the relevant license; the legal representative, main person in charge, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law, be fined not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan, may be prohibited from engaging in corresponding biotechnological research, development, and application activities for a period from ten years to life, and their relevant practice certificates shall be revoked according to law.

Article 75 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, engages in biotechnological research or development activities without complying with national safety management norms for biotechnological research and development, the relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective responsibilities, order correction and give a warning, and may concurrently impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan; if the person refuses to make corrections or causes serious consequences, the person shall be ordered to stop the research and development activities and shall be imposed a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than two million yuan.

Article 76 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, conducts pathogenic microorganism experimental activities not in a laboratory of the corresponding biosafety level, or a high-level pathogenic microorganism laboratory engages in experimental activities involving highly pathogenic or suspected highly pathogenic microorganisms without approval, the competent departments of health and agriculture and rural affairs of the local people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective responsibilities, order cessation of the illegal act, supervise the destruction or delivery of the pathogenic microorganisms used in the experimental activities to a preservation institution, and give a warning; if the act causes the spread or epidemic of infectious diseases or other serious consequences, the legal representative, main person in charge, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions of removal from office or expulsion according to law.

Article 77 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, allows used experimental animals to enter the market, the competent department of science and technology of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than one million yuan; if the illegal gains are more than 200,000 yuan, shall concurrently impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the illegal gains; if the circumstances are serious, the licensing department shall revoke the relevant license.

Article 79 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, without approval, collects or preserves human genetic resources within China or conducts international scientific research cooperation using human genetic resources within China, the competent health department of the State Council shall order cessation of the illegal act, confiscate the illegal gains and the illegally collected or preserved human genetic resources, and impose a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than five million yuan; if the illegal gains are more than one million yuan, shall concurrently impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the illegal gains; if the circumstances are serious, the legal representative, main person in charge, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law and be prohibited from engaging in corresponding activities for five years.

Article 80 Where a foreign organization, individual, or an institution established or actually controlled by them, in violation of the provisions of this Law, collects or preserves human genetic resources within China, or provides human genetic resources within China to overseas parties, the competent health department of the State Council shall order cessation of the illegal act, confiscate the illegal gains and the illegally collected or preserved human genetic resources, and impose a fine of not less than one million yuan but not more than ten million yuan; if the illegal gains are more than one million yuan, shall concurrently impose a fine of not less than ten times but not more than twenty times the illegal gains.

Article 81 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, without approval, arbitrarily introduces an alien species, the relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective responsibilities, confiscate the introduced alien species and impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 250,000 yuan.
Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, without approval, arbitrarily releases or discards an alien species, the relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective responsibilities, order the person to recapture or retrieve the released or discarded alien species within a time limit and impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan.

Article 82 Where an act in violation of the provisions of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if the act causes personal injury, property damage, or other harm, civil liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 83 Where a biosafety illegal act violates the provisions of this Law, but this Law does not provide for legal liability, if other relevant laws and administrative regulations have provisions, those provisions shall apply.

Article 84 Where a foreign organization or individual transports, mails, or carries dangerous biological agents into the country or otherwise endangers China's biosafety, the legal liability shall be pursued according to law, and other necessary measures may be taken.

Article 85 For the purposes of this Law, the following terms mean:
(1) "Biological agents" means animals, plants, microorganisms, biological toxins, and other biologically active substances.
(2) "Major emerging infectious disease" means an infectious disease that appears for the first time in China, or that has been declared eliminated and re-emerges, or that suddenly occurs, causing or potentially causing severe harm to public health and life safety, causing social panic, and affecting social stability.
(3) "Major emerging animal epidemic" means an animal epidemic that occurs for the first time in China, or that has been declared eliminated and re-emerges, or a latent animal epidemic with a high incidence or mortality rate that suddenly occurs and spreads rapidly, posing a serious threat or harm to the safety of livestock production, and possibly causing harm to public health and life safety.
(4) "Major emerging plant epidemic" means a situation where fungi, bacteria, viruses, insects, nematodes, weeds, rodents, mollusks, or others that severely harm plants, occurring for the first time in China or having been declared eliminated, re-cause plant diseases and pests, or where local harmful organisms suddenly occur on a large scale and spread rapidly, causing severe harm to crops, forests, and other plants.
(5) "Biotechnological research, development, and application" means activities such as scientific research, technological development, and application conducted to understand, modify, synthesize, and utilize living organisms through scientific and engineering principles.
(6) "Pathogenic microorganisms" means microorganisms that can invade humans or animals and cause infection or even infectious diseases, including viruses, bacteria, fungi, rickettsiae, parasites, and others.
(7) "Plant pests" means organisms such as fungi, bacteria, viruses, insects, nematodes, weeds, rodents, mollusks, and others that can cause harm to crops, forests, and other plants.
(8) "Human genetic resources" include human genetic resource materials and human genetic resource information. Human genetic resource materials refer to genetic materials such as organs, tissues, and cells containing human genome, genes, and other genetic substances. Human genetic resource information refers to data and other information generated from human genetic resource materials.
(9) "Microbial resistance" means the resistance of microorganisms to antimicrobial drugs, resulting in the inability of antimicrobial drugs to effectively control microbial infections.
(10) "Biological weapons" means microbial agents, other biological agents, and biological toxins, regardless of their origin or method of production, of types and quantities that are not justified for prophylactic, protective, or other peaceful purposes; and also includes weapons, equipment, or delivery vehicles designed to use such agents or toxins for hostile purposes or armed conflict.
(11) "Bioterrorism" means the intentional use of pathogenic microorganisms, biological toxins, or others to carry out attacks, harming human or animal and plant health, causing social panic, and attempting to achieve specific political purposes.

Article 86 Where biosafety information constitutes a state secret, confidentiality management shall be implemented in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on Guarding State Secrets and other relevant state secrecy provisions.

Article 87 The biosafety activities of the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force shall be separately prescribed by the Central Military Commission in accordance with the principles stipulated in this Law.
Article 88 This Law shall come into force as of April 15, 2021.
